questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to go to southern Europe, Milan has courses in English and then Italian culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The school does not do anything social. You have to find social events and Erasmus events by yourself if you want it

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Alright, you just need to know things go slowly and that almost everything is possible about the pick of courses if you just ask enough times

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They confused me with another person and therefore they would not accept my OLA. SO if you have problems with anything just keep writhing them because there might be a mistake

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is hard to find housing. I used spotahome it was okay but not the best, but overall, I felt it was safe

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Start looking as soon as possible. Airbnb is good if you look for a whole apartment, I had a lot of friends there did that but you will have to be in good time.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy but slow

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You just need to sign up for classes after you arrive and you can change the classes un to november
The Italians use the first week to try different classes and then choose after that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write them and they anwser

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress it will work out

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There wasn't that many classes in math in english

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took 21 ETCS at master level and 9 at bachelor level.
The bachelor course had a way easier exam.
The master courses were as my bachelor courses at home I would say.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost no practical sessions and really theoretical. I had 3 oral exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Genetics
Finanza Matimatica (was in english because I was there but is usually in italian)
Mathematically logic
Mathematically modeling for biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Genetics - bachelor courses, only italians, easy to past

Finanza Matimatica (was in english because I was there but is usually in italian), only italian, diffucult exam, but very interesting 

Mathematically logic, a bit boring classes

Mathematically modeling for biology, alright, there is attendance 2/3 to past the class

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I travel a lot that is very nice. From Milan centrale you can go almost everywhere in italy and they also have a lot of flixbussses.
Then I joined the runnigclub Midnight Runners, it is a good place to be active and meet other internationals.

questions.answer: Travel to all over italy. Eat out a lot.

questions.answer: Easy

questions.answer: Hm not really hust talk to them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The apperitivo and going out a lot to eat, drink coffee and hang out

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that milano is the place UCPH send the most exchange student so there are a lot of danish student and people go in groups of 2-8 people and are not that open to meet new people.
Milano is a huge city it can be a bit overwhelming but also really nice if you like it and get to know it
Try to get a place to live close to your campus and be aware there are a lot of different campuses all over the city.
